Pricing model and reserved capacity options
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Time: 15:00 - 15:55 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (Velora Head of Procurement), Daniel Park (Velora CISO), Lena Wu (Velora Legal Counsel), Omar Saleh (Velora CTO)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick intro from our side, I'm Alex Chen, account exec for Redwood Inference. with me is Priya Singh, our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Priya Singh: hi all, quick hello, i'll run through the integration and kms bits after we cover the procurement ask.
[00:28] Maria Gomez: thanks, Alex. we just want to make sure vendor acceptance won't block our Q4 roll out, procurement timeline is tight.
[00:36] Daniel Park: yeah from security side, we need to validate KMS, SSO, SOC2 and things like key custody.
[00:44] Lena Wu: and legal wants to get a head start on DPA redlines, there are a few clauses around data residency and subprocessors that we'll flag.
[00:52] Omar Saleh: hi, i'll be focused on the infra: can you support private VPC or do we need to go hosted initially. also curious re latency SLOs for clinical workflows.

[01:05] Alex Chen: great, scope makes sense. high level — Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity and private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. most enterprise customers start on hosted to pilot and then move to dedicated or private for SLAs and data isolation.
[01:25] Maria Gomez: our procurement policy prefers vendors with SOC2 type 2 and clear KMS integration options; price approvals go to finance but procurement needs the MSA/DPA to be green by 2026-09-30. is that doable?
[01:40] Alex Chen: timeframe is reasonable. we can send our standard MSA + DPA, we do have standard SOC2 and pen-test artifacts; we'll include them. DPA redlines practiced — we can accept most customer redlines except certain indemnity/processing limits, but we'll mark exceptions up front.
[01:55] Lena Wu: can you confirm whether Redwood manages keys by default or if customer-managed keys (CMK) is supported? the DPA needs that spelled out.
[02:06] Priya Singh: yes, we support both models — hosted with Redwood-managed keys, or a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration for Private and Dedicated where KMS/HSM is customer-controlled. there are some caveats around ephemeral cache encryption and tokenization that we'll note.
[02:26] Daniel Park: on BYOK: does Redwood rotate keys or do we? also, HSM vs cloud KMS? we use GCP KMS and need cross-region replication for DR.
[02:38] Priya Singh: customer controls key rotation in BYOK — Redwood has integration layers to call KMS for unwrap/verify. HSM can be supported via dedicated private deployments, but we need to scope network egress and latency. cross-region replication usually handled by your KMS provider; we'll route requests to nearest region to minimize latency.

[02:58] Maria Gomez: SSO — we use SAML 2.0, SCIM for user provisioning, and strict RBAC. is Redwood able to meet SAML + SCIM + enterprise role mapping?
[03:10] Alex Chen: yes SAML 2.0 SSO is supported, SCIM provisioning we support for RBAC groups, and we have tiered roles (admin, dev, observer). we can share our SSO integration guide.
[03:22] Omar Saleh: latency — for clinical scoring we need sustained p95 < 300ms for 512 token context, is that realistic on dedicated?
[03:34] Priya Singh: on Dedicated with optimized kernels we can target p95 under 300ms for typical sequences, but it depends on model choice, concurrency and batching. for strict SLAs customers usually choose dedicated with autoscaling set conservatively.
[03:50] Unk / Speaker 2: (inaudible) — yeah the model and q4 timeline...

[04:10] Lena Wu: contractually we have two primary asks: 1) DPA data residency and subprocessors list, 2) security appendix referencing SOC2 and encryption controls. can Redwood provide a subprocessors list and confirm data centers?
[04:24] Alex Chen: yes we can provide a subprocessors list. for hosted customers we run in multiple cloud regions, we'll provide the list and we can sign a data residency appendix if you need EU-only.
[04:36] Maria Gomez: Velora needs EU data residency for PHI-derived telemetry. is hosted EU-only an option?
[04:43] Priya Singh: yes, we can restrict routing to EU regions for hosted and for full data isolation we'd recommend Dedicated or Private.

[05:02] Daniel Park: on audit logs and traceability — do you offer token-level audit logging, K/V cache purging logs, and access to request traces for incident forensics?
[05:14] Priya Singh: we provide request-level logs with metadata. for Private deployments we can push logs to your SIEM via secure syslog/collector and provide longer retention windows. there are some PII minimization configs we can apply.

[05:42] Alex Chen: pricing and procurement note — hosted is pay-as-you-go, dedicated has reserved capacity with monthly commit discounts. procurement often needs clear committed spend numbers for internal approvals. I can share a pricing sheet with scenarios (pilot vs 6-month commit vs 12-month reserve).
[05:58] Maria Gomez: finance will want week-by-week burn projection for the pilot. can you provide a pilot pricing scenario?
[06:05] Alex Chen: yes we'll include pilot scenarios; we'll also show impact of batching/quantization recommendations which change unit cost.

[06:20] Omar Saleh: technical question — for VPC peering, do you support AWS/GCP VPC peering and private connectivity? also egress IP allowlisting?
[06:30] Priya Singh: we support VPC peering and private connectivity; egress IPs can be provided for allowlisting. for on-prem we support air-gapped deployments but that requires an enterprise package and additional integration work.

[06:50] Maria Gomez: on the MSA, we have a standard change for indemnity caps tied to service availability. what SLAs does Redwood have?
[06:58] Alex Chen: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can share standard SLA language. for hosted free tier we don't promise SLA. specific uptime numbers depend on contract tier and region.

[07:20] Lena Wu: can you walk me through the typical exceptions Redwood takes on MSA/DPA? we want to map internal approvers to risk buckets.
[07:28] Alex Chen: sure, high level: 1) We typically accept DPA processing terms with standard redlines, 2) We push back on unlimited indemnity or unusually broad data processing definitions, 3) We limit liability to contract value often, but for enterprise we can negotiate higher caps. we'll highlight exceptions in a redline doc.

[07:55] Daniel Park: is there an export controls clause? Velora sells in APAC so we need to ensure no prohibited transfers.
[08:03] Alex Chen: yes our MSA includes export control compliance. we'll provide the legal team the current MSA and export control appendix.

[08:20] Maria Gomez: okay timeline recap: we need MSA/DPA draft this week if possible to start redlines. procurement committee meets 2026-09-22. can Redwood commit to providing documents by 2026-09-10?
[08:33] Alex Chen: yes we can target 2026-09-10 for draft MSA + DPA + subprocessors + SOC2 artifacts.

[08:45] Priya Singh: i'll follow up with an architecture diagram showing how BYOK works with GCP KMS, where the KV cache sits and network egress points. I'll also note latency tradeoffs for dedicated vs hosted.

[09:02] Omar Saleh: on the dedicated/private option, we'll want to scope an infra deep dive — networking, firewall rules, HSM placement, and maintenance window expectations. can we schedule that for week of 9/13?
[09:13] Priya Singh: absolutely, schedule is fine. we'll bring infra and security SMEs to that session.

[09:30] Lena Wu: on data residency appendix — can you provide sample wording for PHI-handling and EU-only routing? we might need to include that in the DPA.
[09:40] Alex Chen: yes we'll include a data residency appendix template and mark optional fields for EU-only.

[09:55] Maria Gomez: any competitors or alternatives we should be aware of during procurement? we have internal benching between Bedrock and Anthropic.
[10:03] Alex Chen: competitors mentioned: Anthropic, AWS Bedrock — Redwood differentiates with unified deploy modes and cost/perf controls; we'll provide a short feature/comparison doc but won't push on procurement.

[10:18] Daniel Park: one more security nuance — will Redwood accept customer-supplied encryption keys for ephemeral caches or does any plaintext touch persist disks in your hosted scenario?
[10:29] Priya Singh: ephemeral caches are encrypted in transit and at rest; with BYOK for Private deployments you can control KMS and we can avoid writing plaintext to persistent disks. we'll document the exact flow.

[10:45] Alex Chen: wrapping up — next steps and owners: we'll email the draft MSA + DPA + subprocessors + SOC2 by 2026-09-10; Priya will send the KMS architecture + VPC diagram by 2026-09-09; we'll set infra deep dive week of 2026-09-13; Velora legal will circulate DPA redlines by 2026-09-08.

[11:05] Maria Gomez: that sounds good. any final questions?
[11:09] Lena Wu: none from legal, i'm good.
[11:12] Omar Saleh: no, thanks.
[11:14] Alex Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up after the call with the docs and a calendar invite for the infra scoping session. talk soon.

[11:25] (meeting ends)
